title: Prompt attribute tagging prototype (scratchpad)
content:
Goal: build a compact prompt library that reliably extracts distinctive attributes (product features, sentiment cues, user intent markers) from short user text. Primary target: downstream signal for reranking and routing policies in search/chat features. Constraints: single-turn prompts, <=150 token budget, robust to typos and terse inputs, deterministic-ish for tagging pipelines.

High-level approach notes:
- Use explicit instruction + few-shot examples to anchor tag taxonomy.
- Prefer concise comma-separated tag outputs (machine-friendly). Consider optional 'confidence' tokens (low/med/high) but avoid freeform numbers to keep parsing simple.
- For borderline cases, return TAG_UNSURE to let downstream rule decide.
- Keep taxonomy hierarchical-light: product_feature, sentiment, intent, urgency, domain.

Quick tag taxonomy (working): product_feature: ui, performance, sync, auth, plugin; sentiment: pos, neg, neutral; intent: bug_report, howto, praise, request, complaint; urgency: low, medium, high; domain: billing, onboarding, api, mobile, web

Prototype prompt (template A):
INSTRUCTION: Given the user message, list short tags describing product features, sentiment, user intent, urgency, and domain. Use only tags from the taxonomy. If unsure, include TAG_UNSURE. Output tags as comma-separated values, no explanation.

EXAMPLES:
1) Message: "app crashes when I try to login via Google"
Output: product_feature:auth, intent:bug_report, urgency:high, domain:auth, sentiment:neg

2) Message: "love the new dark mode — great job!"
Output: product_feature:ui, intent:praise, urgency:low, domain:web, sentiment:pos

3) Message: "how do I export embeddings to S3?"
Output: product_feature:sync, intent:howto, urgency:medium, domain:api, sentiment:neutral

Notes on few-shot choices: examples chosen to cover different combos and to show use of TAG_UNSURE implicitly when domain ambiguous.

Alternative compact prompt (template B) for token-constrained path: simple instruction + 2 examples, explicit taxon list appended.

Failure modes observed (experiments Feb 2025):
- Hallucinated tags: model invents domain names (e.g., "cloud-sync" not in taxonomy). Mitigation: append explicit allowed-tags list in prompt; still occasional noise.
- Over-specific tags: maps "login via Google" to product_feature:oauth-google rather than auth. Solution: add normalization examples and prefer base category.
- Missing intent when message is multi-sentence: sometimes picks sentiment only. Mitigation: emphasize must include all 5 categories; return TAG_UNSURE for missing.
- Token budget vs. taxonomy length: long allowed-tag lists cause failure on mobile clients. Workaround: provide abbreviated tag list (3-letter codes) for low-budget route.

Small eval (ad-hoc): 200 labeled chat messages (internal set). Template A precision/recall rough numbers: product_feature P:0.84 R:0.78, intent P:0.88 R:0.82, domain P:0.75 R:0.69. Main error: domain recall low due to ambiguous user wording.

Ideas to improve:
- Add lightweight verifier prompt step: ask model to re-check tags and answer YES/NO for taxonomy compliance; accept only YES.
- Use embeddings-based closest-tag suggestion as prefilter: map message to nearest tag vectors to bias the model with "likely tags" preamble.
- Use constrained decoding via token-level filters in Dedicated serving where available (INF-4123 ticket).
- For production, create a small deterministic rule fallback: regex for explicit words (billing, invoice, login) when model returns TAG_UNSURE.

Open experiments to run:
- A/B: Template A vs B on mobile (n=5k messages) measure downstream rerank CTR delta.
- Test abbreviated codes approach on low-token clients for latency gains.
- Evaluate two-stage: tag generation then canonicalizer that maps rare variants to base taxonomy.

TODO (short-term):
- Clean taxonomy and publish canonical list to shared repo (GH PR draft above).
- Add 50 more edge-case examples focusing on mixed-intent messages and concierge-style requests.
- Wire quick verifier prototype into local runner (see INF-4123).
- Schedule sync with Solutions Eng (Priya) to review false positive billing cases.

Notes to self: keep prompts terse, prioritize machine-parseable outputs, always include TAG_UNSURE as safety. When in doubt, prefer broader tag. Capture examples of repeated failure types to feed into Optimize recommendations later.
